---
title: 'Configure a pipeline in the UI'
status: implemented
description: 'Create a pipeline from a template in Oore when the repository has no workflow file.'
---

Create a pipeline in the Oore web UI when the repository has no Oore workflow
file. The settings stay in Oore. Oore does not add or change any file in the
repository.

## What you need

- A project linked to a repository. See [Create a project](/build/projects/create).
- Project developer, maintainer, instance admin, or instance owner access.

## 1. Open pipeline setup

Open the project's **Pipelines** tab. Select **Set up a build** for the first
pipeline, or **Add pipeline** when the project already has one.

If Oore finds a valid `.oore.yaml` or `.oore.yml` on the default branch, it
offers that workflow instead. Select **Set up manually** only when the
pipeline should ignore the repository file.

## 2. Pick a template

Under **Start from**, select the closest template:

| Template             | What it sets up                                                   |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Android test app** | A debug APK with `flutter build apk --debug`. No signing needed   |
| **Release Android**  | A release Android build with release signing turned on            |
| **iOS + Android**    | Both mobile platforms. Add signing before you run it              |
| **All platforms**    | Android, iOS, and macOS                                           |
| **Custom**           | Android only, with no template commands. Change anything you need |

## 3. Review the settings

Every setting has a default that builds a standard Flutter app. Change only
what your app needs:

- **Basics** for the pipeline name, platforms, Flutter version, and build
  number offset.
- **Build** for commands before and after the platform build, per-platform
  arguments and overrides, environment variables, artifact patterns, and the
  runner.
- **Signing** for Android keystores and iOS certificates or API keys.
- **Triggers** for source events, branch and path filters, schedules, limits,
  and approvals.

**What will run** shows the exact steps the runner
will run with these settings.

A project that points at a repository on the Oore Mac has no source to send
push or pull request events. Its builds start from the UI, the API, or a
schedule.

## 4. Create the pipeline

Select **Create pipeline**.

## Check the result

Oore shows `Pipeline created` and opens **Run build** with the new pipeline
selected. Run a build and check that it ends as **Succeeded** with the
artifacts you expect.

## Troubleshooting

**Oore uses the repository file instead of these settings**

A pipeline whose **Config source** is
**Use repo config if found (.oore.yaml, .oore.yml)** uses the file whenever it
exists at the commit being built. Remove the file, or have this pipeline read
a different path with **Choose a config file**.

**Oore reports that the repository workflow is invalid**

Fix the file. Oore never falls back to the UI settings when the selected file
exists but is invalid.

**Trigger events are unavailable**

Pipelines for a repository on the Oore Mac start from the UI, the API, or a
schedule. Connect [GitHub](/build/sources/github) or [GitLab](/build/sources/gitlab) to
build on pushes and pull requests.

## Next step

[Trigger a build](/build/run/trigger). When the pipeline works, consider
[moving it into `.oore.yaml`](/build/pipelines/oore-yaml).
